⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 973917c5795f7a440d46a15bc5cf8961af9d8703` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a8d6a7bb1fbfc66271539f98b8c3912442c1cdb9` — the merge of head `9fda5d6b1cb80748bd6ff1b433447cfd5294db85` into base `973917c5795f7a440d46a15bc5cf8961af9d8703`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a8d6a7bb1fbfc66271539f98b8c3912442c1cdb9 && git checkout a8d6a7bb1fbfc66271539f98b8c3912442c1cdb9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 973917c5795f7a440d46a15bc5cf8961af9d8703 9fda5d6b1cb80748bd6ff1b433447cfd5294db85 && git checkout -B drift-repro 973917c5795f7a440d46a15bc5cf8961af9d8703 && git merge --no-ff 9fda5d6b1cb80748bd6ff1b433447cfd5294db85

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 973917c5795f7a440d46a15bc5cf8961af9d8703
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 973917c5795f7a440d46a15bc5cf8961af9d8703` → pass the list as

### ① Derived judgments

- **The retirement set — right, with the window stated.** `watchedWriteState` registers an unkeyed middleware on the engine; `executeWithMiddleware` (engine.ts) wraps `find`, `findOne`, `count`, `aggregate`, `insert`, `update` and `delete`, and the middleware bumps its generation in a `finally` around `next()` for every operation on `sys_organization` that is not in `ENGINE_READ_OPERATIONS` — so insert, update (a slug move included) and delete all retire the answer after the driver statement settles, a throw included. `insertMany` is `insert` with `__partialRowErrors` (engine.ts:16596). Every writer of `sys_organization` in this repository writes through the engine: better-auth's organization plugin through `objectql-adapter.ts` (`dataEngine.insert`, `update`, `delete`; `updateMany` and `deleteMany` are per-row engine calls — the `create_organization`, `update_organization` and `delete_organization` doors land there), plugin-auth's boot invariant (`ensureDefaultOrganizationExists`, `ql.insert` under the system context), `ensureDefaultOrganization` in plugin-auth and its organizations-plugin wrapper, and the data door's `update` (the object admits `get`, `list`, `update`). `git grep` at the head finds no raw knex or driver write to `sys_organization` in non-test source; `seed-tenancy-backfill.ts` reads the table by raw SQL and writes other tables. Outside the serving engine: the cli ceremony (`os migrate organization-ownership --apply`, its own process and engine, ordered before boot by the boot guard), cloud's `change_slug` orchestrator (the object's action targets `/api/v1/cloud/organizations/{id}/change-slug`; that code is not in this repository — if it writes through the tenant's REST data door it passes the engine, if it writes the database directly it is a peer write), and any peer replica. For each of those the stale id can GRANT standing to the old Default Organization's surviving grant and WITHHOLD it from the new Default's grant, for at most the 30 s bound or until the next watched write or non-`write` bump on this engine, whichever is first. The commit window is real and named in the code: inside an engine transaction (for example `inAfterAbortUnit`, which wraps a write whose after-hook may abort) the statement settles and the generation moves before the commit, so a read on another connection in that round trip can memoise the pre-commit row under the post-bump generation — stale in either direction until the bound. A rollback after the bump over-invalidates, the safe direction.
- **The cross-replica case — the dev's reading holds; one condition is unstated.** `bridgeAuthzInvalidation` forwards every local non-`remote` bump, `write` bumps on any object included, and the receiving replica bumps `remote`, which the memo honours — so a bridged peer's `sys_organization` write retires the answer in one hop. But `AuthzClusterBridgePlugin` attaches the bridge only when `OS_AUTHZ_GRANTS_CACHE_TTL_MS` is above 0 AND the cluster driver crosses processes (`authz-cluster-bridge-plugin.ts`, the silent arm; `runtime.ts:128` registers the plugin unconditionally). On the shipped default (TTL 0) no bridge is attached and `reportAuthzCachePosture` says nothing, so a default multi-replica deployment's only cover for #21868's delete-and-recreate on another replica is the 30 s bound, silently. The metadata bridge does not help here: `applyRemoteMetadataMutation` bumps `remote` only on a peer's metadata mutation, never on an organization write. Given that, 30 s (A) is the right backstop and C is rightly rejected: the granting direction exists, the card's own "no time-based staleness" target would be C, and the engine's `organizationProbeMemo` (the precedent the card named) accepts unbounded peer staleness. B has no measured need. Whether the default composition owes a boot-time posture line for this memo, in the spirit of the Fork 2 ruling for the grants cache, is the seat's call, named in ③.
- **`undefined` memoised (A) — right.** No organization, or several and none `default`, is a real answer; a stale `undefined` withholds standing (the safe direction), and the insert or slug move that creates a Default Organization passes the seam. Pinned (`undefined` is a real answer and is memoised). The not-registered arm declines before wiring anything (`registryHoldsObject` false → `readDefaultOrganizationId`, which returns `undefined` without a read) — right, since registering the object writes no row the seam would see; pinned (registered later in the same boot, read at once).
- **The failure arm — pinned with teeth.** `tryFind` rethrows an unreachable store as `AuthzStoreUnavailableError`; `memoisedDefaultOrganizationId` has no catch, so the `set` after the `await` is never reached and the next request reads again. The outage pin asserts the 503 envelope, then `reads: [BY_SLUG]` on the next resolution, then a hit. The dev's two ablation variants (catch-to-undefined, memoise-then-rethrow) are each red on this pin; read as claims, consistent with the assertions.
- **The pre-registration window (A) — right, and the boot ordering is true in the code.** The MEASURED pin starts a write with an empty chain, lets the first resolution register the observer and read the pre-write row, and asserts the stale answer stands until the clock passes 30 s. `AuthPlugin.start()` calls `ensureDefaultOrganizationExists` (auth-plugin.ts:825–848) and `kernel:listening` fires after every `start()` (kernel.ts:621–629), so the invariant's insert settles before any request; the observer registers at the first resolution that reads the anchor, so only a `sys_organization` write in flight at that moment reaches the window.
- **Leg 5 generalised (A) — byte-identical in behaviour; no export, census row or pin moves.** `localizationWriteState(ql)` is now a wrapper over `watchedWriteState(ql, localizationWriteStates, LOCALIZATION_CACHE_WATCHED_OBJECTS)`; the body is the former body parameterised (`watched.has`, `ENGINE_READ_OPERATIONS`, `states.set`), with the same unkeyed registration, the same `finally` bump, the same non-`write` epoch subscription and the same `null` poisoning. `resolve-localization-cache.test.ts` is not in the diff. `LOCALIZATION_READ_OPERATIONS` and `LocalizationWriteState` were module-private and the renamed symbols occur nowhere else in the tree (a repo-wide grep at the head returns no hit outside the file).
- **The byte-identity claims hold on the diff.** The hunks are at 941 (appended after `readDefaultOrganizationId`'s closing brace at 942), 1568→1659 (one line of the call site) and 2029 onward (the localization region). `grantAppliesInTenant` (861), `grantOrganizationOf` (890), `grantAnchorsPlatformStanding` (912) and `readDefaultOrganizationId` (934–942) sit at the same lines in base and head and no hunk touches them. The core pins assert the two reads byte-for-byte (`{ slug: 'default' }` limit 1, then `{}` limit 2, system context). The changeset text does not hold sentence by sentence. Every sentence holds except this one: "A peer replica's write is seen through the `remote` and `metadata` epoch bumps the `authz.invalidated` and metadata bridges deliver." Three things are wrong in it. (a) The `metadata` reason is not bridge-delivered: it is plugin-security's local bump on a metadata watch and on the everyone-anchor declaration (`security-plugin.ts:1903`, `:4743`, through `resolveWriteEpochSource`); the metadata bridge's receipt path bumps `remote` (`protocol.ts:8143`). (b) The metadata bridge carries a peer's metadata mutation, never a peer's `sys_organization` write, so that bridge delivers nothing for the write the sentence is about. (c) The `authz.invalidated` bridge is attached only with the grants cache on (`OS_AUTHZ_GRANTS_CACHE_TTL_MS` above 0) and a cross-process cluster driver; on the shipped default a peer's write is seen by no bump at all, and the following sentence's "a peer's write with no bridge attached" is the default case, not an edge. This text ships as `CHANGELOG.md` and is what an operator reads to decide whether the cross-replica window is bridged. The PR body carries the same attribution ("`metadata` (the metadata bridge's receipt path)").

**The route:** replace that sentence with one that is true, for example: "With the `authz.invalidated` bridge attached (the grants cache on, `OS_AUTHZ_GRANTS_CACHE_TTL_MS` above 0, and a cross-process cluster driver), a peer replica's write arrives as a `remote` epoch bump and retires it; every other non-`write` bump (`metadata`, `manual`) retires it too." The next sentence then stands as written. The PR body's `metadata` attribution should be corrected to match. No code moves; the level and the `Clause-②: no` line stand.
